🗄️ Phase 1: SQL + Python Foundations

SQL — Complete Study List

  • INNER, LEFT, RIGHT, FULL OUTER, CROSS, SELF joins
  • Window functions: ROW_NUMBER(), RANK(), DENSE_RANK(), NTILE()
  • Analytical: LAG(), LEAD(), FIRST_VALUE(), LAST_VALUE()
  • CTEs — readable query composition
  • Recursive CTEs — hierarchy, sequences, gaps
  • Pivot & Unpivot — row-to-column transformations
  • SCD logic — identifying latest records with ranking
  • Deduplication — ROW_NUMBER() PARTITION BY pattern
  • ACID properties, TRUNCATE vs DELETE
  • Stored procedures vs Functions — differences
  • Indexes: clustered vs non-clustered
  • Star Schema vs Snowflake vs 3NF
  • Cumulative sums, running totals, moving averages

Python — Complete Study List

  • Data types, loops, conditions, comprehensions
  • OOP: Classes, inheritance, encapsulation
  • Collections: list, tuple, set, dict — differences
  • File handling: CSV, JSON, Parquet with pandas
  • pandas: read, merge, groupby, apply, fillna, dropna
  • requests module — REST API calls + JSON parsing
  • Error handling: try/except/finally
  • Context managers: with statement
  • Serialization: json.dumps/loads, pickle
  • String manipulation — interview coding patterns
  • Database: pyodbc, sqlalchemy connections
  • Generators, decorators, lambda functions
-- SQL: Window function patterns -- Top N per group (most asked interview question) SELECT * FROM ( SELECT emp_name, dept, salary, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY dept ORDER BY salary DESC) AS rnk FROM employees ) x WHERE rnk <= 3; – Cumulative sum SELECT dept, salary, SUM(salary) OVER (PARTITION BY dept ORDER BY hire_date ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) AS running_total FROM employees; – Latest record per key (SCD / dedup pattern) SELECT * FROM ( SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY emp_id ORDER BY updated_at DESC) AS rn FROM employee_history ) WHERE rn = 1;
# Python: pandas DE patterns import pandas as pd, requests, json df = pd.read_csv(‘data.csv’) df.drop_duplicates(subset=[‘emp_id’], inplace=True) df[‘salary’].fillna(df[‘salary’].median(), inplace=True) df[‘full_name’] = df[‘first_name’] + ’ ’ + df[‘last_name’] df.to_parquet(‘clean.parquet’, index=False) # API call resp = requests.get(‘https://api.example.com/data’, headers={‘Authorization’:‘Bearer TOKEN’}) df_api = pd.DataFrame(resp.json()[‘records’])

🎯 Must-Know Interview Questions

Q: Nth highest salary? → DENSE_RANK() = n OR OFFSET-FETCH
Q: RANK vs DENSE_RANK? → RANK skips numbers on ties; DENSE_RANK doesn’t
Q: TRUNCATE vs DELETE? → TRUNCATE: DDL, no rollback, resets identity. DELETE: DML, can rollback
Q: Union vs Union All? → Union removes dupes (slow). Union All keeps all (fast)
Q: List vs Tuple vs Set? → List: ordered mutable. Tuple: ordered immutable. Set: unordered, no dupes

💬 What to Say in Interviews

“I write complex SQL using window functions — DENSE_RANK for top-N queries, LAG/LEAD for period comparisons, and ROW_NUMBER for deduplication and latest-record extraction. In Python I use pandas for data wrangling, handling nulls, type casting, and file format conversions between CSV, JSON, and Parquet.”

⚙️ Phase 2: Apache Spark + Databricks Platform

Spark Architecture — What to Study

  • Driver vs Executor vs Cluster Manager — draw this
  • Lazy Evaluation — transformations build a plan; actions execute it
  • DAG (Directed Acyclic Graph) — Spark's execution plan
  • Narrow vs Wide Transformations — key difference
  • Jobs → Stages → Tasks — how Spark breaks work down
  • Shuffle — what causes it, how to reduce
  • repartition vs coalesce — when to use each
  • cache() vs persist() — storage levels
  • Broadcast join — small table (<10MB) to all executors
  • AQE (Adaptive Query Execution) — Databricks default
  • Data Skew — salting technique to handle
  • groupByKey vs reduceByKey — reduceByKey is faster

Databricks Platform — What to Practice

  • Create free workspace: community.cloud.databricks.com
  • Job cluster vs Interactive cluster — production vs dev
  • Managed vs External tables — data location matters
  • Temp views vs Global views vs Permanent tables
  • Widgets & parameters for parameterized notebooks
  • %run vs dbutils.notebook.run() — scope difference
  • Delta Log: _delta_log folder — JSON transaction files
  • Unity Catalog: catalog.schema.table — 3-level namespace
  • Git integration — connect to Azure Repos
  • Databricks Workflows — job scheduling with dependencies
  • ADLS mount using service principal + Key Vault
  • Autoscaling clusters — min/max worker configuration
from pyspark.sql import SparkSession from pyspark.sql.functions import broadcast, col spark = SparkSession.builder.appName(“DE_Guide”).getOrCreate() # Narrow transformation (no shuffle) df_filtered = df.filter(col(“salary”) > 50000) # Wide transformation (causes shuffle) df_grouped = df.groupBy(“dept”).count() # repartition vs coalesce df.repartition(10) # full shuffle, increase or decrease df.coalesce(4) # no shuffle, decrease only # Broadcast join — avoid shuffle on large table df_large.join(broadcast(df_small), “emp_id”) # Caching for repeated use df.cache() # MEMORY_ONLY df.persist() # MEMORY_AND_DISK — safer for large data

🎯 Must-Know Interview Questions

Q: Explain lazy evaluation → Build plan on transform; execute on action (count/collect/write)
Q: groupByKey vs reduceByKey? → reduceByKey = local combine before shuffle (faster). groupByKey = all to reducer (memory heavy)
Q: Jobs/Stages/Tasks? → 1 Action = 1 Job. Wide transform = new Stage. Tasks = partition count
Q: What is AQE? → Adaptive Query Execution: adjusts plan at runtime — handles skew, join strategy

💬 What to Say in Interviews

“I understand Spark’s execution model — how a DAG forms, how wide transformations like groupBy cause shuffles, and how broadcast joins eliminate shuffle on large tables. I configure cluster autoscaling and cache hot DataFrames strategically to reduce compute time.”

☁️ Phase 3: Azure Data Factory + ADLS Gen2

ADF — Complete Study List

  • Linked Services — connection definitions
  • Datasets — pointer to data structure
  • Activities: Copy, Notebook, Lookup, ForEach, If, Wait, Stored Proc
  • Triggers: Schedule, Tumbling Window, Event-based, Manual
  • Parameterization — dynamic pipelines at scale
  • Metadata-driven: ForEach + Lookup pattern — copy all tables
  • Integration Runtime: Azure IR, Self-Hosted IR, SSIS IR
  • Error handling: retry policy, failure path, skip incompatible rows
  • Data Flows: visual ETL, schema drift handling
  • Key Vault integration — never store passwords in ADF
  • Incremental load: watermark table pattern
  • CI/CD: ARM template → Azure DevOps pipeline
  • Binary copy for large files (3TB+) with Self-Hosted IR

ADLS Gen2 — Complete Study List

  • ADLS Gen2 vs Blob Storage — hierarchical namespace
  • Gen1 vs Gen2 — Gen2 has POSIX ACLs + Blob API
  • Storage tiers: Hot, Cool, Archive
  • Folder structure: landing/ bronze/ silver/ gold/
  • ACLs vs RBAC — fine-grained vs broad access
  • Mounting in Databricks using service principal
  • Why mounting > access keys — security & rotation
  • Lifecycle management policies
  • Encryption: at rest (SSE) + in transit (TLS)
  • Disaster recovery: GRS (Geo-Redundant Storage)
  • Private endpoints + VNet integration
  • Hierarchical namespace — POSIX-style directories
# Mount ADLS Gen2 in Databricks using Service Principal configs = { "fs.azure.account.auth.type": "OAuth", "fs.azure.account.oauth.provider.type": "org.apache.hadoop.fs.azurebfs.oauth2.ClientCredsTokenProvider", "fs.azure.account.oauth2.client.id": "<app-id>", "fs.azure.account.oauth2.client.secret": dbutils.secrets.get("kv-scope", "sp-secret"), "fs.azure.account.oauth2.client.endpoint": "https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant>/oauth2/token" } dbutils.fs.mount(source="abfss://bronze@storage.dfs.core.windows.net/", mount_point="/mnt/bronze", extra_configs=configs) # ADF Watermark incremental load pattern (SQL) – Step 1: Get last watermark – SELECT watermark_value FROM control_table WHERE table_name = ‘sales’ – Step 2: Query source WHERE updated_at > @watermark – Step 3: Copy data to target – Step 4: UPDATE control_table SET watermark_value = @new_max_updated_at

🎯 Must-Know Interview Questions

Q: IR types? → Azure (cloud-to-cloud), Self-Hosted (on-prem), SSIS (legacy packages)
Q: Copy 3TB from on-prem? → Self-Hosted IR + binary copy + parallel copy settings + staging blob
Q: Incremental load in ADF? → Watermark table: store last processed timestamp, query WHERE updated_at > watermark
Q: Store passwords? → Azure Key Vault — never plain text in linked service
Q: Schema drift? → Enable in Data Flow source, use dynamic mappings with @dataset() expressions

💬 What to Say in Interviews

“I’ve built parameterized ADF pipelines using the watermark pattern for incremental loads, and metadata-driven ForEach pipelines that dynamically handle multiple source tables without duplicating pipeline code. Credentials always go in Azure Key Vault.”

🔥 Phase 4: PySpark Deep Dive + Delta Lake

PySpark — Complete Study List

  • SparkSession — entry point for all Spark operations
  • DataFrame API: select, filter, withColumn, alias, cast
  • Joins: inner, left, right, full, semi, anti, cross
  • groupBy + agg: sum, count, avg, collect_list, countDistinct
  • Window functions with WindowSpec — RANK, LAG, LEAD
  • UDFs: @udf decorator — avoid when built-ins exist
  • Null handling: isNull(), fillna(), dropna()
  • Deduplication: dropDuplicates(subset=[...])
  • Schema: StructType, StructField — enforce on read
  • Reading: CSV, JSON, Parquet, Delta, JDBC
  • Writing: overwrite, append, partitionBy
  • Streaming: readStream, writeStream, Auto Loader
  • Row Hash: sha2(concat_ws()) for change detection

Delta Lake — Complete Study List

  • Delta vs Parquet — ACID, time travel, schema enforcement
  • Delta Log: _delta_log/ JSON files + checkpoint every 10 commits
  • MERGE INTO — atomic upsert (insert new, update changed)
  • Time Travel: VERSION AS OF / TIMESTAMP AS OF
  • Schema enforcement vs evolution (mergeSchema option)
  • Z-Ordering: co-locate related data in same files
  • OPTIMIZE: compact small files → larger ones (~1GB)
  • VACUUM: delete unreferenced files (default 7-day retention)
  • SCD Type 1: overwrite with MERGE
  • SCD Type 2: effective_date, end_date, is_current flag
  • Row Hash incremental: SHA2 all columns, merge on key + hash mismatch
  • Delta Live Tables (DLT): declarative pipeline framework
# MERGE INTO — most important DE interview pattern from delta.tables import DeltaTable from pyspark.sql.functions import sha2, concat_ws, current_timestamp # Row Hash for change detection (no updated_at column) df_src = df.withColumn(“row_hash”, sha2(concat_ws(”||”, df.name, df.salary, df.dept), 256)) DeltaTable.forPath(spark, ”/mnt/silver/employees”).alias(“tgt”).merge( df_src.alias(“src”), “tgt.emp_id = src.emp_id” ).whenMatchedUpdate( condition=“tgt.row_hash != src.row_hash”, set={“salary”:“src.salary”, “row_hash”:“src.row_hash”, “updated_at”:“current_timestamp()”} ).whenNotMatchedInsertAll().execute() # Z-Ordering + OPTIMIZE spark.sql(“OPTIMIZE silver.employees ZORDER BY (dept, emp_id)”) spark.sql(“VACUUM silver.employees RETAIN 168 HOURS”) # Time Travel df_v1 = spark.read.format(“delta”).option(“versionAsOf”, 1).load(”/mnt/silver/emp”)

🎯 Must-Know Interview Questions

Q: Delta vs Parquet? → Delta adds: ACID, time travel, schema enforcement, MERGE, optimized layout
Q: Incremental without updated_at? → SHA2 row hash — merge on key + hash mismatch
Q: What is Delta Log? → _delta_log: JSON per transaction, checkpoint every 10 commits
Q: Z-ordering benefit? → Co-locates data in files; Spark skips entire files using data skipping stats
Q: VACUUM? → Removes unreferenced files; default 7-day retention for time travel

💬 What to Say in Interviews

“For incremental loads I use MERGE INTO on Delta tables. When source lacks updated_at, I compute SHA2 row hash across all business columns and merge on primary key plus hash mismatch. For SCD Type 2, I maintain effective_start_date, effective_end_date and is_current columns, closing previous records on update.”

🏗️ Phase 5: Medallion Architecture + Data Modeling

Medallion Architecture — Layers

  • Landing Zone: Files dropped by source, untouched
  • Bronze (Raw): Ingest as-is + audit columns (ingestion_ts, source_file, batch_id). No transformation. Use Auto Loader for streaming
  • Silver (Cleaned): Remove nulls, dedup, type casting, business rules, join lookups. Store as Delta
  • Gold (Curated): Aggregated, business-ready. Fact + Dim model. Optimized for BI/reporting
  • Audit columns: created_at, updated_at, batch_id, source_file, is_active, row_hash
  • Auto Loader: cloudFiles format — detects new ADLS files, exactly-once processing
  • CDC: Change Data Capture — track inserts/updates/deletes from source
  • Idempotency: Running a pipeline twice gives same result

Data Modeling — What to Study

  • Star Schema: Fact + denormalized Dimensions (BI-optimized)
  • Snowflake Schema: normalized dims — more joins, less storage
  • 3NF: fully normalized — OLTP use case
  • Fact table: measures + FK to dims (sales_amount, qty)
  • Dimension table: descriptive attributes (customer, product, date)
  • Surrogate keys: system-generated, source-independent
  • SCD Type 1: overwrite — no history kept
  • SCD Type 2: add row with new version — full history
  • Data Lakehouse = Data Lake + ACID + SQL (Delta enables this)
  • Data Mesh: domain-owned data products
  • Data Vault: hub, satellite, link — highly scalable
  • HLD / LLD: High/Low level design documents
# Auto Loader — Bronze layer streaming ingestion from pyspark.sql.functions import current_timestamp, input_file_name, lit df_stream = (spark.readStream.format(“cloudFiles”) .option(“cloudFiles.format”, “csv”) .option(“cloudFiles.schemaLocation”, ”/mnt/schema/sales”) .option(“header”, “true”) .load(”/mnt/landing/sales/”) .withColumn(“ingestion_ts”, current_timestamp()) .withColumn(“source_file”, input_file_name()) .withColumn(“batch_id”, lit(“2024-01-01”)) ) (df_stream.writeStream.format(“delta”).outputMode(“append”) .option(“checkpointLocation”, ”/mnt/checkpoint/bronze_sales”) .start(”/mnt/bronze/sales”) )

🎯 Must-Know Interview Questions

Q: Explain Medallion Architecture? → Bronze: raw + audit. Silver: cleaned + business rules. Gold: aggregated for BI. All Delta
Q: Fact vs Dimension? → Fact: numeric measures + FKs. Dimension: descriptive context
Q: Star vs Snowflake? → Star: faster reads, denormalized. Snowflake: less storage, more joins
Q: What is Data Lakehouse? → Data lake + ACID + SQL capability = enabled by Delta Lake

💬 What to Say in Interviews

“I implement Medallion Architecture across all projects. Bronze lands raw data with full audit columns for traceability. Silver applies business rules, deduplication using row hash, and type standardization. Gold produces optimized Star Schema Delta tables for Power BI. Auto Loader handles incremental file detection with exactly-once semantics.”

🔧 Phase 6: CI/CD · DevOps · Security · Governance

CI/CD + DevOps

  • Git branching: feature → develop → main (Gitflow)
  • ADF CI/CD: export ARM template from dev, deploy via DevOps
  • Databricks CI/CD: Databricks CLI to deploy notebooks
  • YAML pipelines: build + release in Azure DevOps
  • Approval gates before production deployment
  • Environment parameters: dev, QA, prod linked services
  • Rollback: re-deploy previous ARM template version
  • Airflow DAGs: orchestrate complex pipeline dependencies
  • Unit testing: pytest + mock DataFrames
  • Automated alerts: Azure Monitor + Logic Apps

Security + Governance

  • Azure Key Vault: store all secrets, connection strings
  • Service Principals: app registration for service-to-service auth
  • Managed Identity: Azure-managed SP, no rotation needed
  • RBAC: Storage Blob Data Reader/Contributor roles
  • POSIX ACLs in ADLS Gen2: folder-level permissions
  • Unity Catalog: 3-level namespace governance in Databricks
  • Collibra: data catalog, lineage, glossary, stewardship
  • Azure Purview: automated lineage from ADF + Databricks
  • Data masking: dynamic masking in SQL / ADF Data Flows
  • Audit logs: Diagnostic Settings → Log Analytics
  • HLD/LLD documentation for production readiness
# Read secret from Key Vault in Databricks storage_key = dbutils.secrets.get(scope="kv-scope", key="adls-key") # Unity Catalog — 3-level namespace spark.sql(“USE CATALOG prod_catalog”) spark.sql(“GRANT SELECT ON TABLE silver.employees TO `analyst@company.com`”) # Airflow DAG skeleton from airflow import DAG from airflow.operators.python import PythonOperator from datetime import datetime with DAG(“medallion_pipeline”, start_date=datetime(2024,1,1), schedule_interval=”@daily”) as dag: bronze = PythonOperator(task_id=“ingest_bronze”, python_callable=ingest_bronze) silver = PythonOperator(task_id=“transform_silver”, python_callable=transform_silver) gold = PythonOperator(task_id=“aggregate_gold”, python_callable=aggregate_gold) bronze >> silver >> gold

🎯 Must-Know Interview Questions

Q: ADF CI/CD? → Dev ADF → Git branch → PR → DevOps picks up ARM → deploy QA → approval → prod
Q: Managed Identity vs SP? → Managed = Azure-managed no secret rotation. SP = manual secret management
Q: Unity Catalog? → Databricks governance: 3-level namespace, row/column security, lineage, cross-workspace sharing
Q: What is Collibra? → Enterprise data governance: catalog, lineage, glossary, data stewardship workflows

💬 What to Say in Interviews

“We follow three-environment strategy — dev, QA, prod. ADF changes committed to feature branches, deployed via ARM templates through Azure DevOps with approval gates before production. All secrets in Azure Key Vault, referenced via dbutils.secrets. Lineage tracked in Collibra with upstream/downstream impact documentation.”

🎯 Phase 7: Interview Prep + Project Narration

Weeks 11–12 Daily Plan

  • Every morning: 3 SQL coding questions — timed, no hints
  • Every evening: 2 PySpark pattern questions + explain aloud
  • Weekday mock: 1 system design question + narrate your project
  • Weekend: full 1.5hr mock interview — record yourself
  • Apply to 5+ roles daily once mock scores improve
  • LinkedIn: post 1 technical tip/week — signals expertise
  • GitHub: push all project code with README
  • Target: Tiger Analytics, Tredence, Deloitte, Infosys, Accenture, Cognizant, Wipro, Capgemini

System Design Answer Framework

  • Structure: Source → Ingestion → Storage → Process → Serve → Monitor
  • Always mention: error handling, retry, audit columns, idempotency
  • Always mention: security (Key Vault, RBAC, service principal)
  • Always mention: CI/CD for deployment automation
  • Real-time vs batch: latency requirements drive this decision
  • Default answer framework: Medallion Architecture
  • Know: Synapse vs Databricks vs ADF-only trade-offs
  • Cost optimization: autoscaling, spot instances, storage tiers

💬 3-Minute Master Project Narration Script

"I worked on an end-to-end Azure Data Engineering pipeline handling [domain]. Data ingested daily from [source] into Azure Data Lake Gen2 via parameterized, metadata-driven ADF pipelines — one pipeline handles all tables dynamically. From the landing zone, Auto Loader streamed new files into Bronze with audit columns: ingestion timestamp, source file path, and batch ID. Bronze to Silver applied deduplication via SHA2 row hashing, null handling, format standardization, and SCD Type 2 merge logic using Delta Lake's MERGE INTO. Gold layer materialized aggregated Delta tables in Star Schema for Power BI. Deployment automated through Azure DevOps — feature branches → develop → ARM template to QA → approval gate → production. All secrets managed via Azure Key Vault. Lineage tracked in Collibra."

🎯 Most Commonly Asked Across All Tier-2 Companies

PYSPARK: Lazy eval, groupByKey vs reduceByKey, repartition vs coalesce, broadcast join, UDFs, AQE, incremental without updated_at, caching, null handling, data skew
SQL: nth highest salary, top 3 per dept, LAG/LEAD, cumulative sum, manager comparison, gaps in sequence, deduplication, pivot
DATABRICKS: Job vs interactive cluster, Unity Catalog, Delta logs, SCD 1&2 in PySpark, autoscaling, caching vs persisting, %run vs dbutils.notebook.run
ADF: Incremental load (watermark), IR types, 3TB file copy, error handling, binary copy, metadata-driven pipeline, Key Vault, schema drift
DELTA LAKE: Delta vs Parquet, MERGE INTO, time travel, Z-ordering, OPTIMIZE, VACUUM, schema evolution, DLT
ARCHITECTURE: End-to-end pipeline design, Medallion layers, Data Lakehouse, Synapse vs Databricks, CI/CD, HLD/LLD, Collibra lineage

Project 6 (Wk 11) · Policy Lifecycle + Snowflake

🎯 Master Interview Q&A Bank
Compiled from Tiger Analytics, Tredence, Deloitte, Infosys, Accenture, Capgemini, IBM, JPMorgan, PWC, EY, Cognizant, Wipro question banks
⚡ PySpark — Core Concepts
  • Lazy Evaluation: Transformations build a logical plan; actions execute it. Enables Catalyst optimizer to reorder, push down, and optimize before running.
  • groupByKey vs reduceByKey: reduceByKey = combines locally per partition before shuffle (map-side reduce). groupByKey = sends all to reducer. Always use reduceByKey.
  • repartition vs coalesce: repartition = full shuffle, increase or decrease. coalesce = no shuffle, decrease only. Use coalesce before write to reduce output files.
  • Broadcast join: Copies small table (<10MB default) to all executors. Eliminates shuffle on large table. Use broadcast() hint.
  • Jobs/Stages/Tasks: 1 Action = 1 Job. Wide transform = new Stage boundary. Tasks = partition count per stage.
  • AQE: Adaptive Query Execution — dynamically adjusts plan at runtime: coalesces small partitions, changes join strategy, handles skew. Default in Databricks.
  • Incremental without updated_at: SHA2 row hash → merge on key + hash mismatch. No hash change = no update.
  • Data Skew: Salting — add random prefix to skewed key, repartition, process, aggregate. AQE handles automatically in Databricks.
🗄️ SQL — Coding & Concepts
  • nth highest salary: DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY salary DESC) = n, or OFFSET (n-1) ROWS FETCH NEXT 1 ROW ONLY
  • Top 3 per dept: DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY dept ORDER BY salary DESC) <= 3
  • Cumulative sum: SUM(salary) OVER (PARTITION BY dept ORDER BY hire_date ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING)
  • More than manager: Self-join employees e1 JOIN employees e2 ON e1.manager_id = e2.emp_id WHERE e1.salary > e2.salary
  • TRUNCATE vs DELETE: TRUNCATE = DDL, no WHERE, no rollback, resets identity, faster. DELETE = DML, supports WHERE, can rollback.
  • Union vs Union All: Union removes dupes (slower sort). Union All keeps all rows (faster). Use Union All unless dedup required.
  • Star vs Snowflake: Star = denormalized dims, faster queries. Snowflake = normalized dims, less storage, more joins. Use Star for BI.
  • Gaps in sequence: LAG() to find where current_id - prev_id > 1
🔷 Azure Data Factory — Patterns
  • Incremental load: Lookup watermark → Copy WHERE updated_at > watermark → Update watermark table with new max
  • Metadata-driven pipeline: Config table with source/target mapping → Lookup activity reads it → ForEach loops → Copy with dynamic parameters
  • IR types: Azure IR (cloud-to-cloud), Self-Hosted IR (on-prem/private network), Azure-SSIS IR (SSIS package execution)
  • 3TB from on-prem: Self-Hosted IR + binary copy + staging blob + parallel copy settings + schedule off-peak
  • Error handling: On Failure path → error folder + retry policy + skip incompatible rows + Logic App email alert
  • Schema drift: Enable "Allow schema drift" in Data Flow source + dynamic column mappings using patterns
  • Key Vault: Create AKV Linked Service → reference secret using @{linkedService().secretName} in linked service definition
🏭 Databricks — Platform & Unity Catalog
  • Job vs Interactive cluster: Interactive = long-running, shared, for dev. Job cluster = spun up per job, terminates after, cheaper, for production.
  • Unity Catalog: 3-level: catalog.schema.table. Cross-workspace data sharing. Row/column security. Automated lineage. Centralized governance.
  • %run vs dbutils.notebook.run(): %run = inline in same session (shares vars). dbutils.notebook.run() = separate session, returns string, supports timeout.
  • Delta Log: _delta_log/ = JSON per transaction + checkpoint every 10 commits. Enables ACID, time travel, schema history.
  • cache() vs persist(): cache() = MEMORY_ONLY. persist() = specify level: MEMORY_AND_DISK for large data.
  • Autoscaling: Min/max workers based on pending tasks. ~2min to scale up — don't use for time-critical streaming.
  • DLT (Delta Live Tables): Declarative pipelines with @dlt.table decorator. Auto-handles dependencies, errors, monitoring.
💾 Delta Lake — Advanced Patterns
  • Delta vs Parquet: Parquet = columnar format only. Delta = file format + transaction log + ACID + time travel + schema enforcement + MERGE + streaming.
  • MERGE INTO: Atomic upsert — insert new, update changed, optionally delete. Single atomic operation. Uses matched/not-matched conditions.
  • Time Travel: SELECT * FROM table VERSION AS OF 5 or TIMESTAMP AS OF '2024-01-01'. Used for auditing and debugging.
  • Z-Ordering: Co-locates related data in same files. OPTIMIZE table ZORDER BY (column). Enables file skipping on high-cardinality filter columns.
  • OPTIMIZE: Compacts many small files → ~1GB files. Improves read performance. Run periodically, not after every write.
  • VACUUM: Physically deletes unreferenced files. Default 7-day retention. Running removes time travel ability beyond retention.
  • SCD Type 2: On change: update old record (set end_date=today, is_current=False) → insert new record (start_date=today, is_current=True)
🐍 Python — Coding Questions
  • Palindrome: s == s[::-1]
  • Word count: from collections import Counter; Counter(s.split())
  • Fibonacci: generator: a,b=0,1; while True: yield a; a,b=b,a+b
  • Split name: df['first']=df['name'].str.split().str[0]; df['last']=df['name'].str.split().str[-1]
  • Duplicates in list: [x for x,c in Counter(lst).items() if c>1]
  • Replace vowels: import re; re.sub('[aeiouAEIOU]', ' ', s)
  • Merge dicts: {**d1, **d2} or d1|d2 (Python 3.9+)
  • List vs Tuple vs Set: List=ordered mutable. Tuple=ordered immutable. Set=unordered no dupes.
